description.value: The study investigated structural brain alterations associated with cancer-related PTSD in breast cancer survivors and examined the longitudinal course of right orbitofrontal gray matter volume over two years.

design.value: Baseline MRI scans were obtained in breast cancer survivors with PTSD, breast cancer survivors without PTSD, and healthy subjects. Follow-up scans were obtained 2 years later in a subset of the cancer survivors. Voxel-based morphometry was used for baseline group comparisons, correlations with PTSD symptoms, and repeated-measures analyses of the interaction between diagnosis and measurement time.

description.value: A semi-structured interview, including the clinician version of the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders, was administered by a trained psychiatrist to assess current diagnoses.

A self-reported questionnaire consisting of 15 items, with 7 items assessing intrusion symptoms and 8 items assessing avoidance symptoms. Each item was rated on a 4-point scale: “not at all” = 0, “rarely” = 1, “sometimes” = 3, and “often” = 5.
Cognitive impairment was defined as a score of less than 24 on the Mini-Mental State Examination.

task_name.value: voxel-based morphometry of baseline gray matter volume

task_description.value: Baseline structural MRI scans were analyzed using optimized voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume among cancer survivors with PTSD, cancer survivors without PTSD, and healthy subjects.

task_name.value: longitudinal course of right BA11 gray matter volume

task_description.value: Repeated structural MRI measurements at baseline and 2-year follow-up were used to examine the effects of TIME, DIAGNOSIS, and TIME × DIAGNOSIS on right BA11 gray matter volume in cancer survivors.

instrument.value: 1.5-T MRI unit (Signa Scanner; GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, Wisconsin)

description.value: MRI scans were acquired with three-dimensional spoiled gradient-recalled acquisition of 1.5-mm contiguous sections under the following conditions: field of view = 230 mm, matrix = 256 × 256 pixels, repetition time = 25 ms, echo time = 5 ms, and flip angle = 45°.

An optimized voxel-based morphometry procedure was used. A customized study-specific template set was created, images were spatially normalized and smoothed, tissue was segmented and modulated, and the images were finally smoothed to estimate local gray matter density.

steps.value: A customized study-specific template set consisting of a T1 image and a priori gray, white, and cerebrospinal fluid images was created from brain scans taken from all study subjects.
All scans were spatially normalized to the customized template.
Images were smoothed with an 8-mm full-width at half-maximum smoothing kernel, followed by averaging to create a customized template.
Images were segmented into gray matter and white matter using customized prior probability maps.
The segments were modulated to correct for volume changes occurring during spatial normalization.
The images were smoothed using a 12-mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel.
For the amygdala and hippocampus, 4-mm full-width at half-maximum smoothing was performed before the same procedure was followed.

description.value: Regional brain-volume values were extracted as the β-value of the brain area within the region of interest using the MarsBaR ROI analysis toolbox.

steps.value: The ROI was set within areas detected to be significantly smaller in cancer survivors with PTSD than in those without PTSD at baseline.
The β-value of the brain area within the ROI was extracted as the value indicating regional brain volume.

model_type.value: analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with a basic SPM2 model

model_settings.value: Baseline gray matter volume was compared between cancer survivors with PTSD and those without PTSD or healthy subjects, with age, accumulated alcohol consumption, and total gray matter volume as nuisance variables. Whole-brain significance was corrected using the false discovery rate; hypothesized regions were assessed at an uncorrected p-value of 0.001 with k = 100, with additional small volume correction for bilateral ACC and OFC.
Regional brain volume was correlated with the IES score while controlling for age, accumulated alcohol consumption, and total gray matter volume. Significance levels were set at p < 0.05, two-tailed.

level.value: group-level analysis among cancer survivors with PTSD

model_type.value: repeated measures mixed model analysis of covariance

model_settings.value: TIME, DIAGNOSIS, and TIME × DIAGNOSIS were used as effects on brain volume within the ROI. Age, accumulated alcohol consumption, total gray matter volume at baseline, and days from baseline to follow-up were included as covariates. Significance levels were set at p < 0.05, two-tailed.

model_type.value: repeated measures mixed model analysis of covariance

model_settings.value: A repeated measures mixed model analysis of covariance was also performed using SPM2 software, following the procedure shown in Draganski et al.
Student's t-tests or χ2 tests were used for comparisons of demographic factors to confirm homogeneity between groups; significance levels were set at p < 0.05, two-tailed.
